vignette: Kieu had always taken pride in her independence and self-sufficiency. As a financial analyst, she was meticulous and thorough, traits that served her well in her career. But all of this changed one fateful night when she was held captive by a group of armed men who broke into her home. The memory of those hours, feeling helpless and terrified as they ransacked her belongings and taunted her, still haunted her. As the days turned into weeks, Kieu found herself withdrawing from the world around her. She began to feel that no place was truly safe, except for the confines of her own apartment. Even then, she would lie awake at night, her ears straining for any unusual sound, her heart racing with every creak and groan of the old building. Her thoughts were consumed by a deep sense of shame and contamination, as if the trauma had somehow tainted her very being. She couldn't shake off the feeling that the people who should have protected her - the police, the security system in her building - had all failed her. Kieu's attempts to cope with these overwhelming emotions led her down a path of avoidance and self-blame. She tried hard not to think about the trauma, pushing it deep into the recesses of her mind, but this only seemed to make things worse. Her mind began to wander to alternate scenarios - what if she had been more vigilant? What if she had invested in better security systems? These counterfactual thoughts swirled around her like a maelstrom, making it difficult for her to sleep or concentrate on anything else. As the months went by, Kieu found herself increasingly isolated. Her friends and family grew concerned about her reclusive behavior, but Kieu couldn't shake off the feeling that she was living in a perpetual state of danger. She became convinced that even small setbacks - a spilled cup of coffee, a missed appointment - were harbingers of greater disasters to come. This sense of threat permeated every aspect of her life, making it hard for her to feel safe even in her own skin. As she lay awake at night, Kieu's thoughts would spiral back to the trauma, and she would find herself caught in a cycle of fear and self-blame. She was trapped in this never-ending loop, unable to escape the feelings of contamination and shame that had taken hold of her. It was only when she found herself struggling to make it through the workday without breaking down that Kieu realized she needed help. With a sense of trepidation, she made an appointment with a therapist, hoping against hope that someone could finally help her break free from this prison of fear and self-doubt. Kieu's eyes would often well up with tears as she recounted these events to her therapist. Her voice barely above a whisper, she spoke of the deep sense of institutional failure that still lingered within her - how the very people who should have protected her had let her down so catastrophically. And yet, even in the midst of this despair, there was a glimmer of hope - a recognition that perhaps, just perhaps, there was a way out of this darkness, and back into the light of a life worth living.
